messages.content: what's the color of the sea?

function.name: weather_forecast_get_prediction
function.description: Retrieve weather forecast data for a specified location and date range. The data includes temperature, precipitation, and wind speed. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The location for which to retrieve the weather forecast, in the format of 'City, Country' (e.g., 'London, UK').

start_date.description: The start date for the forecast period in the format of 'YYYY-MM-DD' (e.g., '2023-04-01').

end_date.description: The end date for the forecast period in the format of 'YYYY-MM-DD' (e.g., '2023-04-07').

units.description: The unit system used for the weather forecast. Choose 'metric' for Celsius or 'imperial' for Fahrenheit.

include_details.description: Whether to include detailed hourly forecast data or not. If set to false, only daily summaries will be provided.

message.content:
The sea typically appears **blue**—a result of how water absorbs and scatters sunlight. Water molecules absorb longer wavelengths (red, orange, yellow) more efficiently than shorter wavelengths (blue, green). As sunlight penetrates the ocean, the blue light is scattered back to our eyes, giving the sea its characteristic hue.

However, the exact color can change depending on several factors:

| Factor | Effect on Color |
|--------|-----------------|
| Depth | Deeper water tends to look darker blue or even black because more light is absorbed. |
| Algae & phytoplankton | High concentrations can give the water a greenish tint. |
| Suspended particles | Mud, silt, or sediment can make the water appear brown or murky. |
| Weather & sky | A clear blue sky can reflect onto the surface, intensifying the blue appearance. |
| Sun angle | At sunrise or sunset, the sea may take on reddish or orange hues. |

So while the classic image of the sea is blue, its color can shift dramatically based on environmental conditions.
